lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Hello again, my friend! Last night I went for a long walk under the <color=red>stars</color>, and I quite forgot to come home for supper!

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: It got me thinking up three <color=red>riddles</color> about space. Solve them all and three new books will appear in the library.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 1: I travel around the Earth about once a month. I have no light of my own, but I glow by <color=red>reflecting</color> the sun's light. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. What goes around the Earth and lights up the night sky?

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 2: I am a huge ball of burning gas at the centre of our <color=red>solar system</color>. Every planet travels around me. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which one is hot enough to be made of burning gas?

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 3: I am a planet famous for the beautiful <color=red>rings</color> of ice and rock around my middle. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which planet is best known for its rings?

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Three out of three! You're a true space <color=red>explorer</color>. Three new books are on their way to the library.

afterLines.speaker: Old Barnaby
afterLines.text: On a clear night, look up. If you're lucky, you might spot a <color=red>shooting star</color>. I'll be out there too, if I remember my coat!
